turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Hello there! How's your day treating you?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My friend is colourblind and some of our games are really hard for him.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's thoughtful of you to notice. Is it red and green he struggles with? That's the most common.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yeah, he mixes up those pieces all the time.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: You could add little stickers or marks to one set, like a dot on the green pieces, so they're different by shape too.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: That's clever. Do newer games think about this?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Many do now. Some print symbols next to colours on cards and boards. Reviews often mention whether a game is colourblind friendly.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'll check before I buy anything else.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: And ask him which games bother him most. He'll probably appreciate being asked rather than guessed about.
